methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Candela is a Series C transportation company that has raised €129M+ to date. The valuation landscape for frontier-transport businesses at this stage remains sparse; the addressable peer universe comprises seven private companies including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and ZeroAvia. No public comparables exist in this subsector, limiting traditional public-market benchmarking.

Standard peer-median triangulation is not applicable here. The transportation sector contains only three same-sector candidates globally, and none satisfy the filters required for meaningful statistical comparison—zero companies at the same stage, zero at adjacent stages, and zero within similar valuation tiers. Reliance on all-sector median multiples would introduce excessive noise and obscure the capital intensity and development timelines specific to hardware-focused transportation ventures.

The lack of sufficient comparable data points constrains precision in this valuation. Without viable peer multiples or a dense public-market reference set, analysis would benefit from alternative methods—such as venture capital follow-on pricing, discounted cash flow modeling with sector-specific assumptions, or stage-adjusted benchmarking across the seven private peers on revenue multiples or capital-deployment efficiency. The key uncertainty remains the appropriate risk-adjusted discount rate and terminal-value assumptions for capital-intensive transportation hardware at Series C, where commercialization timelines and regulatory risk vary substantially across subsectors.
